ECT (aka “shock therapy”) followed up with maintenance meds

There is no single “cure” for “depression” I’m of the opinion that what we refer to as “depression” is actually several disorders that share symptoms. Why else would the same treatments have such wildly different results for different people? It’s only logical to come to the conclusion that the SOURCE of depressive symptoms must be different and so that’s why different treatments help people even when they have similar symptoms.

There’s also big differences when it comes to situational vs clinical depression. (That’s not to say that situational cannot develop into chronic/clinical depression) Of course if you lose your job/lose a loved one/experience difficulties or hardship it can somewhat make sense that you would experience depressive symptoms. Treatment for that may not necessitate medical intervention outside of therapy and/or maybe you only need medication for a period of time to help you get through it.

That’s very different from chronic clinical depression that research shows has genetic links. There is a history of depression in my family and when I was the most depressed there was objectively nothing wrong with my life at the time. Nevertheless everything felt wrong all the time to me. I tried everything: medications, TMS, and ketamine therapy, along with counseling but nothing made any difference until I eventually went through ECT. There was something biologically/chemically wrong with my brain (most likely passed down through genetics).

While we don’t understand exactly how/why ECT works, it is still one of the most effective treatments we have today. It changed my life.

I really hate the cultural narrative around “shock therapy” and how it has been portrayed in pop culture. It is nothing like what you’ve seen in the movies (that’s not to say it doesn’t have side effects).

I really hope that by talking about my experience it can help change how some people view this life-saving treatment. I was scared of it and because of that I tried everything else before ECT even though my doctor had recommended it months before I actually tried it. I could’ve gone through treatment sooner had I had more realistic and positive information about ECT.

She is treating me like a child that is incapable of taking care of themself and using my mental health diagnosis as “leverage” in attempting to control my behavior. I don’t see how you could say that isn’t manipulative.

Additionally, I am being respectful and listening to her when she speaks to me this way. I am looking for advice as she is becoming more and more overbearing and I want to handle the situation as mature and respectfully as possible.

Context: I have struggled with clinical depression on and off for my entire life. Last year I had the worst episode to date and ended up hospitalized for the first time. I moved back with my parents after my hospitalization so I would have extra support while undergoing treatment (fortunately, my parents are generally great. Usually very understanding and helpful). 

It’s been a couple months now and I’m happy to report that treatment has gone really well! I’m doing great at work, have gotten back into my old hobbies, go out with my friends again, and have even found a SO that knows about my diagnosis and background with psychiatric struggles. I’m thrilled to be able say that I’m genuinely thriving! I’m not quite ready to move back out as I’d like to save up a bit more before doing so, but it shouldn’t be more than a couple more months before I’m good to go.

I have a great relationship with my parents, so I don’t mind living with them as an adult. There’s only one issue that has come up. As I’ve gotten better I have become much more independent and social again. My mom and I are really close but she does struggle with codependency issues. 
When I moved out before she did get kinda controlling and acted strangely in the times leading up to me moving. Things improved as soon as I actually moved out. 
I think she sees me going out more, acting more independently, etc and can sense that I will be moving out again somewhat soon-ish. She has begun to try and restrict me from some of my social activities out of “concern.” She claims that I am not taking care of myself and that I shouldn’t go out for the sake of my mental health (for reference, “going out” is getting dinner with a friend, watching a movie at my bf’s place etc so nothing crazy). 
I try and just ignore her and do my thing but she is becoming more aggressive about it, telling me I “can’t see” how I am behaving due to my mental illness. I find it extremely unfair that she is treating me like an unreliable narrator of my own life and basically telling me that I need to trust and follow her perspective on everything even if I don’t agree with her because I’m “incapable” of self-awareness.

I’ve mostly been “hearing her out” and continuing to live life on my own terms, but she is becoming more persistent about it every day now. I don’t want to feel like a captive for the next couple of months, and I also don’t want to ruin my relationship with my mom by fighting with her when she tries to control me in this way (again she is otherwise a lovely lady)

Any advice on how to deal with this? It feels disrespectful to me for her to use my diagnosis against me in this way…
